plain: Should Colorado keep mailing a ballot to every active voter, with drop boxes and in-person voting centers, largely as it does now?
agree_means: Agreeing keeps universal mail ballots, drop boxes, voting centers and the post-election audit, with room for smaller fixes.
disagree_means: Disagreeing means a major change, such as ending automatic mail ballots, requiring in-person voting or counting by hand. That would take new laws, polling places and workers.

now.text: A 2013 state law sends a mail ballot to every active voter. Voters can mail it back, use a drop box or vote at a voting center. This year ballots had to go out October 2 to 9; drop boxes open October 12 and centers October 19.

sources.title: Colorado Voting Reforms: Early Results (The Pew Charitable Trusts)
sources.quote: Requiring that mail ballots be sent to all registered voters while still accommodating in-person voting before and on Election Day.

sources.title: Victory for Voters: Supreme Court Determines Postal Service May Not Enact Changes ahead of 2026 General Election (Colorado Secretary of State)
sources.quote: County Clerks are required to send ballots to all voters between October 2 and October 9, 2026. Ballot drop boxes will be available statewide beginning October 12, 2026, and voter centers will be open statewide beginning October 19, 2026.

now.text: In 2024, 92.2% of ballots came by mail. Turnout was 79.5% of active voters and 73.8% of voting-age citizens, versus 64.7% nationally.

sources.title: News Release: Secretary of State certifies the 2024 General Election (Colorado Secretary of State)
sources.quote: Returning a mail ballot was the preferred method for voters with 92.2% of voters choosing to cast their mail ballot during the 2024 General Election

sources.title: 2024 Election Administration and Voting Survey Comprehensive Report (U.S. Election Assistance Commission)
2024 Election Administration and Voting Survey Comprehensive Report (U.S. Election Assistance Commission)
sources.quote: Data from the 2024 EAVS show that 64.7% of the citizen voting age population (CVAP) in the United States voted in the 2024 general election

now.text: Checks include signature review, a copy of ID from first-time mail voters, and a statewide audit of paper ballots after every election since 2017. The state says it has never found an error caused by the voting system.

sources.title: Amendment 84 | ID requirements for mail ballots (Colorado Politics)
sources.quote: Colorado also requires identification for in-person voting, while first-time mail voters must provide a copy of an approved identification document.

sources.title: News Release: 2024 post-election audit complete (Colorado Secretary of State)
sources.quote: The risk-limiting audit has been conducted in every Colorado election since the 2017 Coordinated Election. The audit has never found a discrepancy that was a result of the voting system not working as intended.

stakes.text: Pew's study of the first election under the law found counties spent about $9.56 per vote in 2014, versus nearly $16 in 2008. That data is old, and no newer comparison turned up.

sources.title: Colorado Voting Reforms: Early Results (The Pew Charitable Trusts)
sources.quote: spent about $9.56 per vote in the 2014 general election, compared with nearly $16 in 2008

stakes.text: Going back to polling places would mean more sites and workers. In 2008 Colorado used over 16,000 poll workers at 1,800-plus locations. In 2014, under mail voting, it used fewer than 4,000 at about 300.

sources.title: Colorado Voting Reforms: Early Results (The Pew Charitable Trusts)
sources.quote: In 2008, Colorado had over 16,000 poll workers at more than 1,800 polling locations across its 64 counties

sources.title: Colorado Voting Reforms: Early Results (The Pew Charitable Trusts)
sources.quote: fewer than 4,000 poll workers were employed at approximately 300 voting locations statewide

stakes.text: Provisional ballots, which are used when a voter's eligibility is unclear, fell from 39,361 in 2010 to 981 in 2014. Among mail voters, 95% said they were satisfied with their experience.

sources.title: Colorado Voting Reforms: Early Results (The Pew Charitable Trusts)
sources.quote: The use of provisional ballots declined nearly 98 percent. In the 2010 general election, voters in the state cast 39,361 provisional ballots. In 2014, that number dropped to 981.

sources.title: Colorado Voting Reforms: Early Results (The Pew Charitable Trusts)
sources.quote: Among mail voters, 95 percent indicated that they were satisfied or very satisfied with their voting experience

stakes.text: In March 2026 President Trump directed the Postal Service to build a system that could block ballots to voters not on state-submitted lists. On Sept. 14 the Supreme Court kept a freeze in place, so mail voting works as usual this fall. Colorado was a plaintiff.

sources.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump's proposed mail ballot restrictions for 2026 election (Votebeat)
sources.quote: Trump’s order directed the U.S. Postal Service to set up a new system that would allow the agency to block delivery of mail ballots to voters not on a list presubmitted by state election officials.

sources.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump's proposed mail ballot restrictions for 2026 election (Votebeat)
sources.quote: But as a result of Monday’s decision, mail voting in the 2026 election will largely function the same way it has in previous elections.

sources.title: Victory for Voters: Supreme Court Determines Postal Service May Not Enact Changes ahead of 2026 General Election (Colorado Secretary of State)
sources.quote: On August 26, Colorado joined 24 states and the District of Columbia in suing the United States Postal Service to stop the Postal Service from limiting who can receive a mail ballot.

stakes.text: In 2024 a Mesa County mail carrier and a friend were charged with forging stolen ballots. Signature checks caught 12 of 16; three were counted.

sources.title: Two Mesa County women arrested in alleged fraudulent mail-in ballot scheme (Colorado Politics)
sources.quote: Twelve 12 were caught in the signature verification process, but three have been counted and cannot be reversed

case_for.text: Secretary of State Jena Griswold, a Democrat, says the 2024 audit confirmed the results and that Colorado's layered security makes each election fair, accurate and secure.

sources.title: News Release: 2024 post-election audit complete (Colorado Secretary of State)
sources.quote: Colorado's multilayered security approach ensures that each election is fair, accurate and secure, and that every Colorado voter has their voice heard

case_for.text: Supporters point to lower costs, far fewer provisional ballots and high voter satisfaction since 2013.

sources.title: Colorado Voting Reforms: Early Results (The Pew Charitable Trusts)
sources.quote: Costs decreased by an average of 40 percent in five election administration-related categories.

case_against.text: The Trump administration argued in court that its mail-ballot rules aim to prevent voter fraud. The president has also criticized Colorado's mail system.

sources.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump's proposed mail ballot restrictions for 2026 election (Votebeat)
sources.quote: In court filings, the Trump administration argued that the Postal Service plan was a legal effort by the federal government to prevent voter fraud in the election.

sources.title: Frozen funds, vetoes and lawsuits: Why Colorado says it's in Trump's crosshairs (Colorado Politics)
sources.quote: The president has criticized the state’s mail-in voting system

case_against.text: Supporters of Amendment 84 say signatures alone are not enough. Their measure would keep mail voting but add an ID number.

sources.title: Amendment 84 | ID requirements for mail ballots (Colorado Politics)
sources.quote: Supporters of Initiative No. 362 argue that requiring additional identifying information would strengthen election security and help prevent fraudulent ballots.

unknowns.text: The Supreme Court left open whether the federal mail-ballot rules are legal and could apply in future elections.

sources.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump's proposed mail ballot restrictions for 2026 election (Votebeat)
sources.quote: The ruling leaves open the question of whether the restrictions are legal overall and can be implemented in future elections.

unknowns.text: No statewide count of Colorado mail-ballot fraud cases was found, so how often fraud occurs is not settled here.

research_notes: Pew's study is from 2016 and covers 2014 costs; no newer Colorado cost comparison was found before the search limit ran out. Pew's page returned 403 to scripted fetches. Claude in Chrome was not connected, so I read it in the built-in browser pane, in my own tab (marked via browser); it redirects from pewtrusts.org to pew.org. The Colorado Secretary of State press releases are from a Democratic official's office; facts (dates, counts) are used, not the advocacy language. Colorado's own pages say turnout among active voters was 79.5% (3,240,549 votes); the EAC table shows 3,240,754 votes and the same percent. The statewide count of mail-ballot fraud convictions was not found. 'Hand count' as a change is not covered by a source; I only note the audit is a statistical sample. The Trump order is dated March 31, 2026 in the SoS release; Votebeat says March. The 2013 law's text (HB13-1303) was fetched from the session laws PDF but not quoted.
